chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu Zurara al-Tamimi, from Abu Hassan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When God, Mighty and Majestic, willed to create the earth, He commanded the winds, and they struck the surface of the water until it became waves. Then it foamed, and it became a single unified foam. He gathered it in the place of the House (Kaaba). Then He made it a mountain of foam. Then He spread out the earth from beneath it.
And this is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Verily, the first house established for the people is the one at Bakka, blessed.'
And it was also narrated from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), similar to it.

key_terms.دَحَا: to spread out, to flatten (the earth) — a Quranic term for God's act of making the earth habitable
key_terms.زَبَد: foam, froth — the primordial matter from which the earth's foundation was formed
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ الْبَيْتِ: the place of the House — the site of the Kaaba, understood as the cosmological center

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir narrate about the creation of the earth and the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes the cosmological narrative of the earth's creation: God commanded the winds to stir the primordial waters, which foamed and gathered at the site of the Kaaba, becoming the first solid ground — a mountain of foam from which the earth was then spread out. This hadith links the cosmological event directly to Quran 3:96, establishing the Kaaba as the primordial center of creation and explaining why it is called the 'first house' for humanity. The early Shia audience would have understood this as affirming the sacred centrality of the Kaaba and the cosmic significance of Mecca.
